decisions.reason: The source changes R16/R17/R18 for the three panel button/switch inputs and does not change the separate BOOT button or J_RESET EN-to-GND circuit.
The new pull-ups are GPIO input-bias resistors for panel controls, not I2C SDA/SCL pull-ups or signal-conditioning components.
Changing panel-input polarity and biasing does not alter the ESP32 module model, breakout coverage, breakout placement, or header pitch.
The source changes electrical bias and pressed behavior but does not reassign any GPIO or change the GPIO-compatibility policy.
The source concerns panel-control inputs and explicitly separate PIR/touch input biasing, not the e-paper backlight supply, PWM control, or switching circuit.
Connecting three input-bias resistors to the existing 3.3V rail does not change the specified DCDC1 voltage or regulation requirement.
The panel-input bias correction does not change which rails are monitored, the monitoring IC, channel allocation, or measurement coverage.
The source does not change the standalone regulator, its capacity, source-selection behavior, or powered load.
The active-low panel inputs are unrelated to the addressable-LED power cutoff GPIO and MOSFET switching topology.
The source changes schematic connectivity for R16/R17/R18 but specifies no resistor value, package, population, or part-number change that necessarily modifies the assembly BOM state.
The source confirms PIR and touch outputs are active-high with pull-down input biasing, but it does not change the requirement to use 3.3V-compatible sensor logic without an on-board level shifter.
The source changes panel button/switch input biasing and confirms no change for PIR/touch biasing; it does not alter the sensor-module connector inventory or pinouts.
